title: CWRU vs Lehigh: tuition, size, location
summary: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) versus Lehigh University (Lehigh). Also searched as Lehigh vs CWRU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Lehigh University and Case Western Reserve University (Lehigh vs CWRU) are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Lehigh University is located in Bethlehem, while Case Western Reserve University is situated in Cleveland. The undergraduate enrollment at Lehigh is approximately 5,898 students, compared to 6,437 at Case Western Reserve. Tuition for in-state students at Lehigh is $64,980, slightly lower than the $66,608 charged by Case Western Reserve. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Lehigh University and Case Western Reserve University (Lehigh vs CWRU) have similar tuition rates for both in-state and out-of-state students, with Lehigh charging $64,980 and Case Western Reserve charging $66,608. The median debt for students who complete their programs also differs slightly, with Lehigh graduates carrying a median debt of $21,960, while Case Western Reserve graduates have a median debt of $24,000. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each institution.

Lehigh vs CWRU shows that while tuition costs are close, the median debt upon graduation is somewhat lower at Lehigh University. This comparison helps prospective students understand the potential financial impact of attending either university.
